assessments.reasoning: The Classpath project’s rendered source identifies the class and release in its title and the FSF in the copyright notice. All four captures share the claimed source digest and cover bytes [0,60183) contiguously. The operative passage is at source lines 27–37.

The License Index’s own SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7, bytes [640,783), admits additional permissions or documented modifications to a base license. The Classpath linking grant satisfies the additional-permission criterion.

challenge.method: Under SCES-1.0 §§3–4 and Protocol stage 7, tested whether the text merely describes linking, and whether its grant would cover a module derived from the library. Policy commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710, adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce.
challenge.results: The copyright holders expressly grant permission after describing linking. They define an independent module as one neither derived from nor based on the library, require compliance with each such module’s license, and give modifiers a choice about extending the exception. Those boundaries support the scoped identity.

limitations: Lines 7–10 name GPL version 2 and separately give the recipient a later-version election. Affected base editions are a separately scoped question.
The finding covers this file notice. Other files, OpenJDK designations, modified libraries and particular applications require their own evidence.
reasoning: GNU Classpath 0.95 identifies Package.java as part of the library. Lines 22–25 describe the GPL treatment of a combination. Lines 27–37 then grant conditional permission to link independent modules and distribute the executable. That additional permission meets the Index criterion for a license exception. The registry value active is editorial. Applicability to a particular executable depends on its facts.
